correctness.rationale: For n>=3 every shortest-path interval is classified explicitly: cross-shore nonmatching edges have no internal vertices; same-shore distance-two intervals cover precisely opposite vertices avoiding both indices; matched-index opposite-shore distance-three intervals cover the graph. The iff criterion follows, including one-shore and mixed-shore boundary cases. Minimality and all-set enumeration are then exhaustive with disjoint families. The standalone independent BFS/interval verifier exhaustively confirmed the iff and both polynomials for 349497 subsets over n=3,...,9; this finite check supports but does not replace the proof.

Actual scientific-index searches and published-source queries under crown, K2 tensor Kn, deleted perfect matching, geodetic polynomial and minimal geodetic sets found no theorem implying the complete iff and both polynomials. value.rationale: The result is a complete structural and coefficientwise classification for a standard connected vertex-transitive regular bipartite family, not a singleton calculation or numerical extremum. It determines both all-set and minimal-set distributions, constructs an unbounded upper-minus-lower geodetic gap n-2, and exhibits the three-point minimal cardinality spectrum {2,6,n} with arbitrarily long missing intervals. These are motivated by the gap between prior scalar strong-geodetic results and exact ordinary geodetic enumeration.
